construct: a border-color EQUAL to the bare control element's (a library global like shadcn's `* { border-color: var(--border) }` styles the control too) on a part that draws a real border
why: The styled-channel door subtracts the control, so a global reset that reaches the control erases the subject's base border colour — shadcn.select shipped border style+width with NO base colour, the CSS surface still painted via border-color's currentColor initial-value rule, and the canvas drew NO stroke at all (the rejected census set: a bare trigger with no box). Equality with a control that draws no border proves library authorship, not absence.

canvas.note: the 2px border strokes on canvas with the carried colour — width and style alone paint nothing there
